title: The Wildcard Default Fallback (Match Silence)
pattern: Using a catch-all wildcard (like `_` in Rust or `default:` in C) to group and silently execute default fallback behavior for all unlisted variants of an enumeration.
why_bad: When new states/variants are added to the enum in the future, the compiler will not flag this `match` statement as incomplete. The new state will be silently funneled into the default fallback branch (e.g., a newly added `Reconnecting` state would unexpectedly stop all activity), creating logical bugs that are hard to detect.
detection: Match expressions on closed enumerations that use a wildcard (`_`) default branch instead of list-exhaustion.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Permissible on open, highly volatile external integer representations, but highly dangerous on internal state enums.
fix: Explicitly list every enumeration variant in the match arm, allowing the compiler to enforce exhaustive checking when new variants are introduced.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete*, Section 8.6 / 8.7 (offensive programming: default case should fail hard during development to expose unhandled states).
